These stacktraces depend on a lot of factors. It's a bit of a race condition what's the exact stack trace. Is the resource cached or not? How fast was the fs access? What's the last operation?

I think it's better to exclude them from the snapshot, i. e. replace them with a `STACK TRACE` label.

This test case depends on the type of filesystem (case-sensitivity or not?).

Here is how you could test it: https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/master/test/cases/errors/case-sensitive/test.filter.js

Either skip the test on the wrong filesystem or offer two alternative snapshots depending on filesystem

so, my reason for rewriting these tests:

- while debugging this, the older tests were a bit unrevealing & cryptic
- improvment on previous `getErrors`/`getErrorsPromise` approach
- using inline snapshots because i think it really makes sense for these - and will reveal things that previous tests did not.. such as when more warnings/errors are emitted than expected.
- 1 compile per test (not good to run all use cases in a single test, imo)
- we should probably add some tests covering fatal errors (aka thrown) - any advice welcome
